title: Memory & Melody

agents.function: Research programme histories, build original nostalgia-led rundowns; no presenter imitation.
Discover singers and recordings; distinguish albums, soundtracks, singles, compilations and reissues.
Credit communities, performers and languages; connect local and global listening routes.
Keep publisher, geography, period and methodology together; never present an old snapshot as live.
Build timed editorial plans and review audio/recording rights.
Plan music-video discovery and source/rights checks; support local user-owned video preview.

items.title: cold/mess
items.summary: The cited 2020 re-release differs from the 2018 EP described by the catalogue. Keep edition dates separate.

items.title: G.O.A.T.
items.summary: A 2020 Diljit Dosanjh album in the cited catalogue; a regional-to-global discovery entry, not a present-day rank.

items.title: Katchi Sera (From Think Indie)
items.summary: A Sai Abhyankkar single from 2024. Keep singles separate from full albums.

items.title: Radical Optimism
items.summary: Dua Lipa’s 2024 album; a modern listening reference, not a claim that this is her latest release.

items.title: GOLDEN
items.summary: Jung Kook’s 2023 album; artist market and sung language are separate fields. Do not confuse it with the HUNTR/X song Golden.

items.title: I Told Them...
items.summary: Burna Boy’s 2023 Afro-fusion album. Regional editions and clean/explicit versions need individual checks.

items.title: Marathi songs · Arnold Bake Collection
items.summary: The catalogue credits Madhumalati and Sneha Dhopeshwarkar and includes Palna, Mangalagaur Arati and Hadga. Historical recording/catalogue dates must not imply an open licence.

items.title: Music of Goa
items.summary: The source describes Zagor, Ranmale, Dhallo, Fugdi and Gudulyo Gayan in distinct community and performance contexts. Avoid flattening these into a single generic folk style.

items.title: Bengal · folk and classical connections
items.summary: A source-backed route through Baul, bhatiyali and the relationship between folk and classical traditions. Recording permissions and community context remain essential.

items.title: Folk Music of India · regional archive
items.summary: A historical collection spanning several Indian regions, not a complete or neutral representation of every community. Preserve named performer credits when available.

items.title: World traditions · open discovery map
items.summary: The Folkways world catalogue offers routes into Caribbean, Celtic, Central Asian, African American, Indigenous and other traditions. These are discovery categories, not one universal genre or a complete world atlas.

items.title: Billboard Hot 100
items.summary: US songs chart; separate from global songs and album charts. No current positions cached.

items.title: Billboard 200
items.summary: US albums chart; album rankings are not song rankings. No current positions cached.

items.title: Billboard Global 200
items.summary: Songs ranked using streams and sales from over 200 territories, including the US; not simply a global radio-airplay chart.

items.title: Billboard India Songs
items.summary: India Songs appears in Billboard’s territory-chart directory. Open the publisher for its available issue and methodology; no current entries imported.

items.title: Official UK singles & albums
items.summary: Separate singles and albums rankings with publisher-specific sales/streaming rules. Check the chart period; no fixed weighting formula is hard-coded here.

items.title: Spotify charts & Local Pulse
items.summary: Platform-specific streaming charts; city popularity and Local Pulse are distinct. Not every stream is chart-eligible, and daily/weekly periods differ.

items.title: YouTube songs, videos & Shorts
items.summary: Songs aggregate eligible song views across formats; video charts rank official music videos. Shorts are a separate metric. Paid advertising views are excluded.

items.title: IFPI Global Single Chart · 2025
items.summary: A dated annual snapshot, published 19 February 2026. Not a live chart or this week’s top songs.

items.title: Audio · radio, interviews & listening notes
items.summary: Original spoken introductions, oral-history interviews with consent, instrumental/classical sessions, podcasts and playlists are proposed production formats. A timed rundown is not a rendered or broadcast episode.

items.title: Video · performance, visualiser & documentary
items.summary: Music-video discovery, live-session commentary, original visualisers, interviews and captioned documentary plans. Lyrics, concert footage, artwork, sync and master-use permissions must be reviewed separately.

items.title: Hate You · music video
items.summary: A separately catalogued music video, not the album audio recording. Provider access, region and use rights must be checked.

items.title: Big 7 · music video
items.summary: A music-video catalogue reference. The storefront link is not a licence to embed, download or rebroadcast the footage.

items.title: Katchi Sera · music video
items.summary: The video catalogue credits these names; verify vocal, lyric, performance and production roles separately. This is distinct from the audio single.

items.title: Tum Hi Ho · soundtrack recording
items.summary: A track-level catalogue reference linking Arijit Singh and Mithoon to the Aashiqui 2 recording. A soundtrack track is not a solo studio album.

items.title: Qawwali — the mehfil ensemble
items.summary: The best-known South Asian Sufi music form: a lead singer with a chorus, harmonium, tabla and dholak, building a piece through repetition and call-and-response. We keep the ensemble structure and the credit rules; we never import a shrine recording. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Kafi — Punjabi and Sindhi devotional verse
items.summary: A sung verse form used across Punjab and Sindh for Sufi poetry, carried by Bulleh Shah and the Sindhi tradition. A kafi cycle sets us a sequence and a theme, not a tune to copy. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Amir Khusrau — the Persian-Hindavi bridge
items.summary: The poet-musician tradition credits Khusrau with shaping both qawwali practice and the Hindavi-Persian poetic bridge that later ghazal and khayal singing inherit. History and attribution, not a text we reuse. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Mehfil and sama — the listening gathering
items.summary: The gathering format around the music: a sequence that opens with praise, moves through poetry, and closes on repetition, with the audience inside the performance rather than in front of it. This is the structure our original mehfil programme borrows. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Sufi rock and fusion — the modern route
items.summary: From the 1990s onward, bands and producers set devotional poetry inside rock, pop and electronic arrangements, which is how this repertoire reached a new audience. A lineage to document and credit, and a production style we may study for our own recordings. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Baul — Bengal's wandering minstrels
items.summary: Bengali minstrel singers with ektara and dotara, singing of the divine in the everyday. A distinct regional route into the same devotional material, and a reminder that one Sufi reading is never the only one. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Ghazal — form and structure
items.summary: A poem in couplets with a fixed refrain and rhyme pattern, each couplet standing on its own, which is exactly why a ghazal survives being sung out of order. The grammar our original ghazal cycle is written in. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Ghazal gayaki — gharanas and the thumri tie
items.summary: Classical ghazal singing carries gharana technique — Banaras, Lucknow and Patiala among the thumri schools — which is why the same couplet sounds different in different hands. Technique families to name and credit, not recordings to reissue. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Ghazal poetry — the Urdu line
items.summary: The sung ghazal begins as literature: a line of poets from the Deccani works through the Delhi and Lucknow schools to the twentieth century. We keep the chronology and the attribution, and we commission our own verse rather than republishing theirs. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Begum Akhtar — thumri and ghazal gayaki
items.summary: A reference point for how semi-classical technique and recorded ghazal met: trained across more than one gharana, and equally at home in thumri, dadra and ghazal. Studied for phrasing and sequencing; her records stay hers. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Mehdi Hassan — the classical concert ghazal
items.summary: The concert stage where classical ghazal gayaki reached a mass audience, and the reference for how a long programme holds a hall. A model for programme shape, with every recording credited to its own rights holders. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Ghazal today — records, television and the mehfil revival
items.summary: How the form travelled — shellac-era records, the film and television ghazal, then the concert and festival circuit and the small-room revival. The route map for our own cycle, with no recording rehosted at any stop. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Coke Studio Pakistan — house band and guest artists (from 2008)
items.summary: The format we are learning from: a house band with guest artists, recorded live in a studio, season by season under a named producer. The cited account lists the first season in 2008 and fifteen seasons by the check date, with production passing from its founders to later producers. Format and history only. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: The Coke Studio format beyond Pakistan — India, Bangla, Bel 3arabi
items.region: South Asia / Middle East / Brazil origin
items.summary: The same studio-collaboration idea in other countries: the Pakistani edition began in 2008, India in 2011, an Arabic edition in 2012 and a Bengali edition in 2022, with the concept traced back to a Brazilian project in 2007. A comparative map of how one format adapts to a language and a market. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Coke Studio India — 2011 launch and the regional variants
items.summary: The Indian edition opened in 2011 with a first season of long-form episodes and a television tie-in, then returned in several different shapes and, later, regional editions. Evidence that an Indian-language version of this format is viable - and that it needs its own identity rather than an imported one. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Coke Studio Bangla — a language-first edition (2022)
items.summary: The Bengali edition launched in 2022 and is the closest recent example of the format being rebuilt around one language and its own musicians rather than translated into it. The model we intend to follow for Hindi and Marathi. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: MTV Unplugged — the acoustic session format
items.summary: An artist plays their own material with acoustic arrangements in a controlled room: no spectacle, performance front and centre, and editions localised per country. A low-risk format for our first recorded sessions, because it needs a room and a band, not a set. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: The Dewarists — collaboration as documentary
items.summary: Two musicians from different traditions are paired to write and record something new, and the episode documents the process as much as the song; its makers describe it as part music documentary, part travelogue. The closest structural ancestor to what we want our original collaborations to be. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Tiny Desk Concerts — the intimate single-take session
items.summary: One small space, one continuous performance, the artist choosing the set: proof that a music programme needs no studio budget to travel. The template for the first Vyomaraj sessions, scaled to a room we actually have. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: What we may inherit from these shows — and what we may not
items.summary: Format, structure, sequencing and production method are reference material. Titles, lyrics, audio, video, artwork, logos and episode content are never copied, and nothing is rehosted. Any future licensed use requires a written licence naming the rights holder. Every card in this group follows that rule, and so does every plan the planner can build from it. Format context only: no episode, recording, lyric, artwork or brand asset is imported, copied or rehosted.

items.title: Original: Mehfil Sessions — our own gathering format
items.summary: The first original programme in this lane: a four-part gathering that opens with praise, moves through poetry and closes on repetition, with an original scripted link at every step and a source line for every reference. Built on the mehfil structure above; it contains no borrowed verse, melody or recording.
items.rights_basis: Original script, sequence and links written for Vyomaraj and credited to named creators before release; no third-party work is sampled, adapted or rehosted.

items.title: Original: Sufi Cycle — nine nights of devotional programming
items.summary: Nine original programmes, one per night, each taking a single devotional theme through poetry, commentary and an original composition, with regional variants (Punjabi kafi, Bengali Baul, Deccan) night by night. Written for Vyomaraj; nothing existing is performed or reissued.
items.rights_basis: Original compositions and scripts to be written, credited and recorded by named Vyomaraj creators; no existing composition, lyric or recording is used.

items.title: Original: Ghazal Cycle — new verse in the mehfil setting
items.summary: A ghazal programme built the other way round from a covers show: the verse is written first for Vyomaraj, then set and sung, with credit for poet, composer and performer on every piece. The classical forms above are the grammar, not the material.
items.rights_basis: Original verse and compositions commissioned for Vyomaraj with named writers, credited before release; no existing couplet, melody or recording is used.

items.title: Original: Navaratri 2026 cycle — nine nights, one programme each
items.summary: The launch programming for the Navaratri window that opens on Ghatasthapana, 11 October 2026, and closes at Vijayadashami on 20 October 2026: nine original programmes, one per night, each pairing a devotional theme with a music or ghazal set and its own credits. Ties the bhakti lane to this one, and is the programme the 11 October live run is meant to open with.
items.rights_basis: Original programme plan, scripts and compositions produced by Vyomaraj for the 2026 Navaratri window; festival timing follows public almanac references, and no third-party work is used.
